findings.headline: High stress at lap 31 coincides with early soft‑tyre fatigue – consider earlier pit or driver break
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 87.8 on lap 31 while the driver was on a 20‑lap soft tyre set (age 20) and still leading. The model shows a slight degradation (+0.057 s/lap) but pace delta rose to +0.147 s, indicating the stress‑fatigue link triggered the first strategy warning. A short rest or earlier pit could prevent the later larger stress spikes.

findings.headline: Stress spike at lap 58 did not hurt pace – no pit change needed
findings.detail: Stress rose to 79.9 on lap 58 while on a soft tyre set (age 10) that was still modelling a small negative degradation (‑0.057 s/lap). Pace delta dropped to –0.207 s, showing no loss despite stress. The strategy rule correctly logged an INFO hold, confirming the driver can maintain performance under stress at this stage.

findings.headline: Intermediate tyres struggled on drying track – consider harder compound or earlier wet switch
findings.detail: From laps 63‑71 the driver switched to intermediate tyres (age 13‑11) while the track cooled to 20 °C and rain returned. Pace delta rose sharply to +3.777 on lap 67, the worst of the stint, matching the modelled degradation of +0.844 s/lap for the final intermediate set. This suggests the intermediate compound was too soft for the drying track; a harder compound or earlier switch to wets could have limited the time loss.

findings.headline: Blue‑flag periods on intermediates caused no significant pace loss
findings.detail: During laps 7‑10 the driver was blue‑flagged while on intermediate tyres (age 5‑8) on a drying surface. Pace delta stayed within ±0.5 s, indicating the driver managed traffic without losing time despite the extra workload.

findings.headline: Early stress spike on lap 2 while on softs in wet – watch for repeat after tyre swaps
findings.detail: The driver’s stress reading of 69 on lap 2 coincided with the first wet‑track laps on soft tyres (age 2) and a 1.2 s gap to car ahead. No pace delta is recorded, but the early high stress may reflect grid‑to‑track adaptation; monitor for similar spikes after future tyre changes.

findings.headline: Rapid stress rise between laps 30‑31 correlates with slight pace loss – flag for fatigue monitoring
findings.detail: From lap 30 to 31 stress jumped from 23.2 to 87.8 while the driver was still on a soft set (age 19‑20) and the track was dry. The pace delta increased from +0.011 to +0.147, hinting at a rapid fatigue onset. With only two data points this pattern is tentative, but it aligns with the strategy’s fatigue monitor at lap 31.
